title: "Offloading" Undergraduate Research to the Graphics Processing Unit for Acceleration
problem: Undergraduate research in physics/engineering traditionally requires years to master PDE formulation; making advanced research accessible requires both education and performance.
motivation: N-body simulations accessible to freshmen can democratize physics research; modern GPUs enable this on consumer hardware.
method: Reformulate PDEs as N-body simulations; leverage GPU acceleration on gaming desktops for undergraduate research projects.
key_novelty: Pedagogical approach to making advanced physics research accessible via GPU-accelerated N-body methods.
contributions: Framework for reformulating PDEs as N-body simulations
Demonstration that consumer GPUs enable meaningful undergraduate research
Educational pathway requiring only freshman-level math and CS knowledge
limitations: Educational focus rather than technical contribution; limited experimental results; narrow scope.
